text: Handling out-of-order events — a real problem, and a different one from lateness.
Last lesson's watermark deals with events arriving too late entirely. Out-of-order is different — events arrive within tolerance, just not in the sequence they actually happened in.
Ingestion time minus event time shows exactly how stale each event was on arrival. It doesn't fix anything by itself — it just makes the gap visible so you can decide if it matters.
Most aggregations like count and sum genuinely don't care about order — tolerate it. If order does matter, widen the watermark. And genuinely problematic events can be routed elsewhere for review.
Sorting a finished window's output doesn't fix how it was computed — that's a display fix, not a computation fix. Next up: eventstream transformations, shaping data as it flows.
